open_points.subject: clock.monotonic_ns deadline start
open_points.text: The caller derives a bounded wait's deadline from it — the reading at the start plus the bound
open_points.question: At what exact event is the initial reading taken for a sandbox execution and for an HTTP request: before setup, immediately before launching/writing, or at another defined point?
options: Include sandbox environment creation and request-send setup in the bounded interval
Start immediately before the sandbox process is launched or the HTTP transport begins
Let each caller define its own start point
open_points.default_guess: Take the initial reading immediately before launching the sandbox process or beginning the HTTP transport.

open_points.subject: clock.monotonic_ns deadline boundary
open_points.text: asks whether it passed with a later reading
open_points.question: Is the wait expired when the later reading is equal to the deadline, or only when it is greater than the deadline?
open_points.default_guess: Treat equality as expired: reading >= deadline.

open_points.subject: clock.monotonic_ns host source
open_points.text: Return one reading of the host monotonic clock.
open_points.question: Which host monotonic clock must back the operation, particularly whether elapsed time during system suspend counts toward deadlines?
options: Use Python time.monotonic_ns / the platform CLOCK_MONOTONIC equivalent
Use a suspend-aware monotonic source such as CLOCK_BOOTTIME where available
Any nondecreasing host clock is conforming
open_points.default_guess: Use Python time.monotonic_ns consistently on every platform.
